children: Indian benchmark indices are likely to see a muted start on September 2, tracking GIFT Nifty, which was trading flat at around 24,042.50 in early trade.

Indian equity indices ended marginally lower for the second consecutive session on September 1 amid volatility, as buying in FMCG, IT, media and metal stocks was offset by selling across auto, banking, pharma and realty names.
At close, the Sensex was down 12.99 points or 0.02 percent at 76,944.28, and the Nifty was down 24.60 points or 0.10 percent at 24,055.80.
The broader market underperformed the benchmark indices, with Nifty midcap index falling 1.4 percent and smallcap index down 0.2 percent.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Flat)
GIFT Nifty was trading with little change at around 24,042.50 in early trade, indicating a flat start for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Equities (Slip)

Stocks slumped at the start of the Asian trading session on Wednesday as a bond market-induced panic on global markets spilled over into the region, after renewed attacks by the US on Iran pushed oil prices higher.
US Equities (Down)
U.S. stocks extended their slide on Tuesday, as the ​global bond selloff deepened and crude prices spiked amid fading hopes for a near-term solution to the US-Israeli war with Iran.

The Dow Jones Industrial ​Average fell 418.97 points, or 0.79%, ⁠to 52,766.93, the S&P 500 lost 54.67 points, or 0.71%, to 7,631.47 and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 271.11 points, or 1.03%, to 26,099.77.
Dollar Index (Up)
The dollar held firm on Wednesday as renewed hostilities in the Middle East pushed oil prices higher and revived inflation concerns.
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, was at 99.74.
US Bond Yield (Up)
The Treasury 10-year yield advances to the highest since late 2023 as rising oil prices exert inflationary pressure.
Asian currencies (Mixed)

Asian currencies traded mixed against the dollar, with the South Korean Won rising 0.27%. The Indonesian Rupiah fell 0.12%, while the Japanese Yen declined 0.08%. The Philippines Peso dropped 0.28%, followed by the Taiwan Dollar at 0.11%, Thai Baht at 0.08%, China Renminbi at 0.06%, Malaysian Ringgit at 0.05% and Singapore Dollar at 0.02%.
Crude (Up)

Oil prices rose nearly 1% in early trade on Wednesday, extending the previous session's surge, as concerns over supply disruption intensified after the U.S. and Iran exchanged strikes overnight, dimming hopes for a quick easing of tensions in the Middle East.
Gold (Down)
Gold held a decline as attacks in the Middle East and a global bond selloff ratcheted up bets the Federal Reserve may need to raise interest rates to rein in inflation.
Fund Flow Action

On September 1, Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) snapped their three-day selling streak and turned net buyers, purchasing equities worth Rs 1,143 crore. Meanwhile, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) continued their buying activity, investing Rs 1,846 crore in Indian equities during the session.
